why: The answer explains the reason for the whole strategy: if you compile after every few lines, any error is close to the code you just wrote, so it is easy to find. That is the relational point that small steps keep debugging local.

concepts.quote: each error is next to the code you just wrote, so it is easy to find
concepts.why: It links small steps to debugging by making the newest change the first place to look for an error.

concepts.quote: If you compile after every few lines
concepts.why: It treats compiling correctly as the step that finds errors but adds no rule or relation about javac.

concepts.quote: each error is next to the code you just wrote
concepts.why: It only implies that compiling catches errors in the source, without applying this to how javac reports them.
The answer says nothing about reading or interpreting the compiler's messages.
The answer makes no claim about the source file or its name.
